question.text: Which of the following shaded regions corresponds to the domain of the function $f(x,y) = \dfrac{1}{x^2 - y}?$
question.explanation:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following condition is satisfied:

  • The expression in the denominator is not equal to zero.

As a result, the points in the domain must satisfy the following inequality:

\[ x^2 - y \neq 0 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad y \neq x^2 \]

Therefore, the domain is

\[ D = \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, y \neq x^2 \big\}. \]

question.text: Find the domain of the function $f(x,y)= e^{x^2-y^2}.$
question.explanation:
Notice that

  • $x^2-y^2$ is defined for all $x$ and $y,$ and

  • $e^{g(x,y)}$ is defined if $g(x,y)$ is defined.

As a result, $e^{x^2-y^2}$ is defined for all values of $x$ and $y.$ This means that the domain of $f$ is the entire $xy$-plane.

example.title: The Domain of a Function Containing Exponential, Logarithmic, and Trigonometric Functions

question.explanation:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following conditions are satisfied:

  • The expression in the denominator is not equal to zero, and

  • the expression under the square root is non-negative.

As a result, the points in the domain must satisfy the following inequality:

\[ x+2> 0 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x > -2 \]

Therefore, the domain is

\[ \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\,:\, x > -2 \big\}. \]

example.title: The Domain of a Function Involving Reciprocals and Radicals

question.explanation:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following conditions are satisfied:

  • The expression in the denominator is not equal to zero, and

  • the expression under the square root is non-negative.

As a result, the points in the domain must satisfy the following inequalities:

\[ \begin{cases} x-y \geq 0 \\[5pt] x^2 + y^2-4 > 0 \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} x\geq y \\[5pt] x^2 + y^2 >4 \end{cases} \]

Therefore, the domain is

\[ \big\{ (x,y)\in\mathbb R^2 \,:\, x \geq y, \: x^2 + y^2 > 4 \big\}. \]

question.text: The function $f(x,y)$ is defined as \[ f(x,y) = x\sin{y}. \] Evaluate this function at the point $\left(-6,-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right).$
question.explanation:
To evaluate our multivariable function at the point $\left(-6,-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right),$ we substitute $x = -6$ and $y = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ into the function expression:

\begin{align*} f\left(-6,-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) & = x\sin{y} \, \Big|_{(-6,-\pi/4)} \\[5pt] & = -6\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\\[5pt] & = -6\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\\[5pt] & = 3\sqrt{2} \end{align*}
